docs.title: trappy-inator
docs.text:
trappy-inator is the template and project that every Trappy-Scopes instrument starts from.

The name is actually inspired by a cartoon called Phineas and Ferb, which has a comical villain, Dr. Heinz Doofenshmirtz, who is very funny and who names everything with the suffix "-inator". His first machine was actually called an Inator, so this is like a wordplay.

This website is the showcase for that template. Every Trappy-Scopes instrument keeps its 3D-printed parts as parametric OpenSCAD source files. From those files the website is built automatically: printable STL and 3MF files, a 3D view of every part and assembly, a bill of materials, and assembly and disassembly instructions. Every part carries its version, so the exact file you printed can be linked and cited.

To show the whole workflow on something small, this project contains a single model: a to-scale facsimile of Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, the green alga at the centre of our work. Its cell body, eyespot and two flagella are separate parts that together form one assembly.

The Catalog shows each part with its files. In the Playground you can change every parameter of the cell, from its shape to the length of each flagellum, and see the result in 3D straight away. OpenSCAD runs in your own browser, so the model you download is generated from exactly the parameters you chose. The Notes explain how the files, renders and citations are produced, and how to build your own project from this template.

docs.title: Parts
docs.text:
View in 3D Flagella

The two flagella (cilia), about 0.25 µm thick and 10–12 µm long, leaving the cell on either side of the papilla. The cis flagellum is the one nearest the eyespot. Both beat in one plane; the model shows them at the start of the power stroke.

trappy-inator:chlamydomonas · part flagella · rev …

Tunable: length of each flagellum, diameter, exit spacing, exit angle, bend.

STL · Open in the Playground

View in 3D Eyespot

The orange-red light sensor: layers of carotenoid globules, about 0.6–1.5 µm² in area, near the cell equator on the side of the cis flagellum. In the model it stands slightly proud of the surface so it can be seen and printed in its own colour.

trappy-inator:chlamydomonas · part eyespot · rev …

Tunable: length, width, thickness, angle from the beat plane, height from the equator, tilt.

STL · Open in the Playground

View in 3D Cell body

A prolate cell about 10 µm long and 8 µm wide, optionally egg-shaped and narrower towards the flagella, with the papilla between the two flagella. The eyespot sits in a pocket on its surface.

trappy-inator:chlamydomonas · part cell · rev …

Tunable: length, width, anterior taper, papilla height and width.

STL · Open in the Playground

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
How trappy-inator works and how to use it for your own project. These notes only appear on the trappy-inator site; projects made from the template replace them with their own.

Note Read it when you want to know How it works where the 3D files, previews and 3D views come from, for parametric and plain STL parts, and how the Playground runs OpenSCAD in your browser GitHub Actions what happens on GitHub after every push, step by step, and what to do when a run fails Project layout what every folder and file in the repository is for Make your own how to start a new project from this template and add your parts, pages and Playground Porting existing projects how to move an existing project into this layout, with plumbing (parametric) and trappyframe (STL files) as worked examples Versions and citations how parts are named and versioned, and how to cite a part or a configuration Licences and credits what the licences allow and which projects this is built on

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text: GitHub Actions is GitHub's build service: a fresh Linux machine that runs a list of steps every time something happens in the repository. Here it turns the source files into the website. The whole recipe is one file, .github/workflows/site.yml. This note goes through it line by line.

docs.title: When it runs
docs.text:
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 3 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
Trigger When Why push to main every time you push the website always matches the latest source schedule every night at 03:00 UTC changes to the shared look (theme, viewer) reach the site even when the project itself did not change workflow_dispatch when you press Run workflow on the repository's Actions tab to rebuild by hand, e.g. after changing the Pages settings

Pushes to other branches do not publish anything, so you can work on a branch without changing the live site.

docs.title: Permissions and order
docs.text:
permissions:
  contents: write
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true
  • contents: write lets the workflow push the finished website to the gh-pages branch. It never writes to main: only people do that.
  • concurrency makes sure only one build publishes at a time. If you push twice quickly, the older build is cancelled and only the newest is published.
  • No secrets or tokens are needed; GitHub gives the workflow a temporary token for its own repository.

docs.title: The steps
docs.text: The job runs on ubuntu-latest, a clean Linux machine created for this run and thrown away afterwards. Nothing is kept between runs.

docs.title: 1. Check out the repository
docs.text:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0

Copies the repository onto the machine. fetch-depth: 0 fetches the full history, because each part's revision is "the last commit that changed this part's folder", and that needs the history.

docs.title: 2. Set up Python
docs.text:
- uses: actions/setup-python@v5
  with:
    python-version: "3.12"

Python runs the STL-to-GLB converter and MkDocs.

docs.title: 3. Install OpenSCAD
docs.text:
env:
  OPENSCAD_VERSION: 2026.11-RC1

Downloads the official OpenSCAD AppImage for that version from files.openscad.org, checks it against its published SHA-256 checksum (the build stops if it does not match), and unpacks it. It also installs xvfb, a virtual screen, because OpenSCAD needs one to draw preview images on a machine without a display.

To move to a newer OpenSCAD, change OPENSCAD_VERSION here and the version and checksum in tools/fetch_openscad_wasm.sh (the browser build used by the Playground), so both stay the same version.

docs.title: 4. Build the models
docs.text:
- name: Build models
  run: xvfb-run -a tools/build_models.sh

Runs tools/build_models.sh (see How it works). For each parametric part it writes the STL per colour body, the coloured 3MF, the parameter list, the preset file, a copy of the .scad for the Playground, the 3D models and the preview images. For each folder in cad/frozen/ it copies the STLs and makes their 3D models and previews. It also records each part's revision. Everything goes to docs/generated/.

--hardwarnings makes OpenSCAD treat warnings as errors, so a failed assert() in a part stops the build instead of publishing a broken model.

docs.title: 5. Fetch OpenSCAD for the Playground
docs.text:
- name: Fetch OpenSCAD for the Playground
  run: tools/fetch_openscad_wasm.sh

Downloads OpenSCAD compiled to WebAssembly (about 3 MB, checksum-verified) into docs/assets/playground/openscad/. Visitors' browsers load it from the website when they open the Playground.

docs.title: 6. Build and publish the website
docs.text:
- name: Build and publish site
  run: |
    pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
    mkdocs gh-deploy --force

Installs MkDocs, Material for MkDocs and the diagram plugin at the versions in requirements-docs.txt, builds the website, and pushes it to the gh-pages branch, replacing the previous version. GitHub Pages then serves that branch at https://trappy-scopes.github.io/<project>/ within a minute or two.

docs.title: Setting it up once per repository
docs.text:
1. Push the repository with .github/workflows/site.yml in it. The first run creates the gh-pages branch.
  2. In the repository settings, open Pages and set Source to Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root).
  3. GitHub Pages on a private repository needs a paid GitHub plan; on a free plan, make the repository public.

docs.title: When a run fails
docs.text:
Open the repository's Actions tab, click the failed run, then the red step. The log shows the error.

Failing step Usual cause Fix Install OpenSCAD the version in OPENSCAD_VERSION no longer exists on files.openscad.org change it to a current release and update the checksum in tools/fetch_openscad_wasm.sh Build models an assert() failed or the .scad has an error run tools/build_models.sh on your computer, fix the part Fetch OpenSCAD for the Playground checksum mismatch after changing the version copy the new SHA-256 from the .sha256 file next to the download Build and publish site a page links to a file that does not exist, or a package version changed run mkdocs build locally and read the warning

A failed run publishes nothing, so the live site keeps the last good version.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: GitHub Actions is free for public repositories. A run takes a few minutes, mostly installing OpenSCAD and Python packages.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: Where the 3D files come from, how the website shows them, and how the Playground changes them in your browser.

docs.title: Two kinds of part
docs.text:
Kind Source in the repository Example What the build makes Parametric an OpenSCAD file (.scad) the Chlamydomonas cell, the pump box STL per colour body, coloured 3MF, 3D model, preview image, parameter list; editable in the Playground Frozen a finished STL, e.g. exported from Fusion 360 the trappyframe plates the same STL for download, 3D model, preview image; not editable

Both kinds are versioned the same way (see Versions and citations). A frozen part can be converted to OpenSCAD later; until then it is shown and cited exactly as it is.

docs.title: From source to website
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  A[".scad file(parametric)"] --> C["OpenSCAD"]
  F[".stl file(frozen)"] --> C
  C --> D["STL / 3MF downloads"]
  C --> G["Preview image"]
  C --> H["3D model (GLB)"]
  A -.-> P["Parameter list"]
  D & G & H & P --> I["Website"]
  B["git push"] --> R["GitHub Actions"] --> C
  1. You change a .scad or .stl file and push to GitHub.
  2. GitHub Actions runs tools/build_models.sh with OpenSCAD.
    • Parametric parts: OpenSCAD renders one STL per colour body (each can be printed in its own filament), a coloured 3MF of the whole assembly, the parameter list with its ranges, and a preview image.
    • Frozen parts (cad/frozen/<part>/*.stl): the STL is copied for download as it is. OpenSCAD imports it only to draw the preview image and to produce a clean binary STL for the 3D model. An optional file cad/frozen/<part>/colour (one line, e.g. #3A3A3A) sets its display colour.
  3. tools/stl_to_glb.py joins the STLs into one GLB, the format the viewer reads, with one named, coloured node per part. Normals are smoothed on curved surfaces and kept sharp at edges.
  4. MkDocs builds the website around those files and publishes it to the gh-pages branch. Generated files are never committed to main, so the repository holds only sources and every file on the site comes from the commit it describes. The site is also rebuilt every night, so changes to the shared look reach it without a push.

docs.title: How the website shows models
docs.text:
Showcase. A page shows the prebuilt GLB with Google's <model-viewer>. The preview image appears first; the 3D model loads when you ask for it. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, right-drag to pan. Hovering a part name highlights that part.

Playground (parametric parts only). OpenSCAD itself runs in your browser, compiled to WebAssembly, on your own computer; nothing is sent to a server.

  1. The form is generated from the part's parameter list, so it works for any OpenSCAD file written in the Customizer format (below). There is no code written per part.
  2. Moving a slider renders a quick draft with coarser curves; letting go renders full quality.
  3. The result is converted to GLB in the browser (docs/assets/playground/glb.js) and shown in the same viewer.
  4. Colours never need a re-render: the viewer recolours the parts directly.
  5. Downloads are generated in your browser from exactly the parameters you chose.

The browser build of OpenSCAD is the official WebAssembly release from files.openscad.org, checked against its published checksum.

docs.title: Writing parameters
docs.text:
Parameters use OpenSCAD's own Customizer format, which desktop OpenSCAD also understands:

/* [Flagella] */
// The flagellum nearest the eyespot (µm)
cis_flagellum_length = 12; // [0:0.5:20]
  • /* [Flagella] */ starts a group, which becomes a tab in the Playground. /* [Hidden] */ hides what follows.
  • The comment on the line above becomes the description. Put only the range after the value, or OpenSCAD ignores it.
  • [min:step:max] becomes a slider; [a, b, c] becomes a drop-down list.
  • Name parameters so they read as their own label: cis_flagellum_length is shown as "Cis flagellum length". No abbreviations; units go in the description.
  • Set curve smoothness only through $fa and $fs (in the Hidden group), never with $fn on individual shapes. The Playground overrides $fa/$fs to draw quick drafts.
  • Colours are text parameters holding a hex colour ("#4C8C3A"); the Playground shows them as colour pickers.

docs.title: Make your own
docs.text: How to start a new Trappy-Scopes project from this template and customise it.

docs.title: 1. Create the repository
docs.text:
On GitHub, open Trappy-Scopes/trappy-inator and choose Use this template → Create a new repository. Clone it.

Then edit:

  • README.md: one line on what the project is, then a few paragraphs.
  • mkdocs.yml: site_name, site_description, site_url, repo_url, repo_name, copyright. Leave the theme, markdown_extensions and extra_javascript blocks as they are; they are the shared Trappy-Scopes look.
  • Delete docs/notes/ and its entry in nav, and delete cad/parts/chlamydomonas/.

docs.title: 2. Add your parts
docs.text:
A parametric part. Create cad/parts/<part>/<part>.scad.

  • Write parameters in the Customizer format (see How it works).
  • If the part has several colours or filaments, give it a part parameter that selects each colour body (part = "assembly"; // [assembly, body, lid]) and a colour parameter for each. The Chlamydomonas file is a complete example.
  • Optional presets go in cad/parts/<part>/<part>.json (OpenSCAD parameter sets).

A plain STL part. Copy the file to cad/frozen/<part>/<file>.stl. Add cad/frozen/<part>/colour with a hex colour if it should not be grey. Use short, stable folder names (base-plate, not Base Plate 6.3mm (FSSBTv3) v2); the version comes from git, not from the file name.

Then list your parts in tools/build_models.sh. The Chlamydomonas section shows the commands for a parametric part; frozen parts are found automatically.

docs.title: 3. Show them on the website
docs.text:
Showcase. Copy the <model-viewer> block from docs/index.md and change the file names. For a frozen part the files are generated/frozen/<part>/<file>.glb and .png:

<div class="ti-viewer" markdown="0">
  <model-viewer src="generated/frozen/base-plate/base-plate.glb" reveal="manual" camera-controls
      touch-action="pan-y" shadow-intensity="0.8" tone-mapping="neutral" alt="Base plate">
    <div slot="poster" class="ti-poster">
      <img src="generated/frozen/base-plate/base-plate.png" alt="Base plate">
      <button class="md-button md-button--primary ti-reveal"
          onclick="this.closest('model-viewer').dismissPoster()">View in 3D</button>
    </div>
  </model-viewer>
</div>

On pages below the site root (for example bom.md, which becomes /bom/), start the paths with ../.

Playground. Open docs/assets/playground/playground.js and edit the CONFIG block at the top:

Field Meaning name the file name of the part, e.g. pumpbox id how the part is cited, e.g. plumbing:pumpbox parts the colour bodies: the part value in the .scad and the parameter holding its colour hidden parameters not shown in the form (at least part) draft the coarse $fa/$fs used while dragging

Everything else (tabs, sliders, links, downloads) is generated from the .scad file.

Bill of materials, assembly, disassembly. Edit docs/bom.md, docs/assembly.md and docs/disassembly.md as normal Markdown.

docs.title: 4. Publish
docs.text: Push to main. GitHub Actions builds the models and the website and publishes it to the gh-pages branch. Once, in the repository settings, set Pages → Source to the gh-pages branch, root folder. The site appears at https://trappy-scopes.github.io/<project>/.

docs.title: What not to change
docs.text: The theme, colours and viewer settings are shared by every Trappy-Scopes site. Change them here, in trappy-inator, so all sites follow; a project that changes them locally drifts away from the others.

docs.title: Porting existing projects
docs.text: How to move an existing Trappy-Scopes project into this layout. Two worked examples cover the two kinds of part: plumbing (all parametric) and trappyframe (all STL files from Fusion 360).

docs.title: General steps
docs.text:
1. Create the new repository from the template (Make your own), or copy the template files (mkdocs.yml, requirements-docs.txt, tools/, docs/, .github/, .gitignore, LICENSES/) into the existing repository.
  2. Move parts into cad/parts/ (OpenSCAD) or cad/frozen/ (STL).
  3. Delete generated files from the repository (exported STLs of parametric parts, renders, sliced .3mf plates). They are rebuilt by GitHub Actions; sliced plates can be attached to a GitHub release instead.
  4. Move existing documentation pages into docs/ and fill in nav in mkdocs.yml.
  5. Build locally (Project layout), check every page, push.

docs.title: Example: plumbing (parametric)
docs.text:
Today: pumpbox.scad makes several parts through a part parameter (box, lid, oring, assembly, stack), named configurations live in STL file names (box_n4_stag.stl), and BOM.md, TESTPLATES.md, tests/ and print_profiles/ sit at the top level.

Today Moves to pumpbox.scad, pump_proxy.scad cad/parts/pumpbox/, cad/parts/pump-proxy/ configurations in STL names (n4_stag, rec30) presets in cad/parts/pumpbox/pumpbox.json stl/*.stl, renders/*.png deleted; rebuilt by GitHub Actions fonts/ cad/fonts/ (the font licence stays with it) BOM.md docs/bom.md TESTPLATES.md, docs/decode.html docs/ pages (the snap-code decoder works unchanged as a page) tests/, tools/, print_profiles/ stay; tests/ can run in GitHub Actions

Playground: CONFIG.name = "pumpbox", CONFIG.parts = box, lid and O-ring, each with its colour parameter. Before that, the Customizer comments in pumpbox.scad need the new layout (description on the line above, only the range after the value), and short names such as head_w and gp should be renamed so they read as labels.

docs.title: Example: trappyframe (STL files)
docs.text:
Today: eight plates and two block templates exported from Fusion 360, with the version in the file name (Mid Plate Magnets 6.3mm (FSSBTv2) v14.stl), sliced plates in print_files/, and a working MkDocs site with Assembly, Bill of materials, Calibration and Disassembly pages.

Today Moves to frame/Mid Plate Magnets 6.3mm (FSSBTv2) v14.stl cad/frozen/mid-plate/mid-plate.stl frame/Base Plate 6.3mm (FSSBTv3) v2.stl cad/frozen/base-plate/base-plate.stl … one folder per plate cad/frozen/<plate>/ with colour = #1E1E1E for black PLA frame_templates/*.stl cad/frozen/<template>/ print_files/*.3mf (about 95 MB) attached to a GitHub release, removed from the repository docs/assets/Cluster v4.gltf (60 MB) replaced by a compressed GLB of the cluster docs/notes/*.md docs/ with the same tabs version numbers in file names (v14) the git revision; the old number can be noted once in the commit that moves the file

No Playground until a plate is redrawn in OpenSCAD; the 3D views, previews and downloads work straight away. When a plate is converted, it moves from cad/frozen/ to cad/parts/ and keeps its name, so links and citations stay valid.

Dark parts on a dark page

Black plates are hard to see on the dark theme. Use a mid-grey display colour (e.g. #5A5A5A) in the colour file; it changes only how the part is shown, not the files you download.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
Every Trappy-Scopes project uses the same layout. Only the source files are committed; everything the website shows is generated from them.

<project>/
├── README.md                         short introduction; also the top of the website's home page
├── mkdocs.yml                        website: name, tabs (nav) and the shared Trappy-Scopes theme
├── requirements-docs.txt             Python packages for building the website
├── LICENSES/                         full licence texts (hardware, software, docs)
├── cad/
│   ├── parts/<part>/                 parametric parts
│   │   ├── <part>.scad               parameters + geometry, in OpenSCAD's Customizer format
│   │   └── <part>.json               optional named presets (OpenSCAD parameter sets)
│   └── frozen/<part>/                plain STL parts (e.g. Fusion 360 exports)
│       ├── <file>.stl                one or more STL files, committed as they are
│       └── colour                    optional display colour, e.g. #3A3A3A
├── docs/                             the website's pages
│   ├── index.md                      home: includes README.md, then the showcase
│   ├── assembly.md                   assembly instructions
│   ├── bom.md                        bill of materials
│   ├── disassembly.md                disassembly instructions
│   ├── playground.md                 the Playground page
│   ├── notes/                        notes like these (only on trappy-inator)
│   ├── assets/                       logo, showcase and Playground scripts
│   └── stylesheets/extra.css         shared look of viewers, tags and the Playground form
├── tools/
│   ├── build_models.sh               runs OpenSCAD for every part → docs/generated/
│   ├── stl_to_glb.py                 STL files → one GLB for the 3D viewer
│   └── fetch_openscad_wasm.sh        downloads the browser build of OpenSCAD for the Playground
└── .github/workflows/site.yml        GitHub Actions: build models, build the website, publish to gh-pages

docs.title: Generated, never committed
docs.text:
These folders are created by the build and listed in .gitignore:

Folder Made by Contains docs/generated/ tools/build_models.sh STL/3MF downloads, GLB models, preview images, parameter lists, revision of each part docs/assets/playground/openscad/ tools/fetch_openscad_wasm.sh OpenSCAD compiled to WebAssembly build/ both intermediate files site/ mkdocs build the finished website

docs.title: Building the website on your computer
docs.text:
You need OpenSCAD (2026.11 or a recent development snapshot) and Python 3.

tools/build_models.sh
tools/fetch_openscad_wasm.sh
pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Set OPENSCAD=/path/to/openscad if OpenSCAD is not on your PATH.

docs.title: Naming and versions
docs.text:
Every part has a fixed name and two version markers:

Marker Example Set by Changes when Name trappy-inator:chlamydomonas the author: project, then part never; a renamed part keeps its old name as an alias Generation g1 the author, by hand the part no longer fits older versions (its mating dimensions or interfaces change) Revision a1b2c3d git, automatically the last commit that changed the part's own files

The revision is read from git when the website is built and shown under each model. It covers only the part's own folder, so a part that has not changed keeps its revision while the rest of the repository moves on, and its STL stays byte-identical. This works the same for parametric parts (cad/parts/<part>/) and STL parts (cad/frozen/<part>/).

docs.title: Citing a part
docs.text:
Chlamydomonas facsimile (trappy-inator:chlamydomonas, rev a1b2c3d), https://github.com/Trappy-Scopes/trappy-inator/tree/a1b2c3d/cad/parts/chlamydomonas

The link points at the exact commit, so it always shows the files as they were.

docs.title: Citing a configuration
docs.text:
A Playground link records only the parameters you changed. Together with the part name and revision it describes exactly one model:

Chlamydomonas facsimile (trappy-inator:chlamydomonas, rev a1b2c3d), configured at https://trappy-scopes.github.io/trappy-inator/playground/?cis_flagellum_length=8

The Playground shows this line under Cite this configuration, ready to copy.

docs.title: Releases (planned)
docs.text: Each release of a project will be archived on Zenodo, which gives it a DOI. A paper can then cite the release DOI together with the part name and revision.
